newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks turn lower in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks turn lower in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices reversed early gains to fall slightly in late Thursday trade as most sectors fell despite gains in electronics, brokers said.
With 53 minutes left, at 0308 GMT, the index was down 22.30 points or 0.25 percent at 8,934.11, off a high of 9,045.35.
Brokers said investors turned cautious after the finance ministry said on Wednesday it had no immediate plans to raise the ceiling on foreign ownership of Taiwan stocks.
"Apparently the government is trying to cool the market further, but buying on electronics still continues," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.
Electronics were up 1.96 percent, with chipmaker Winbond up T$3.5 to T$58.5 and computer giant Acer up the daily seven percent limit to T$108.

"I've noticed that during recent electronics surges, very few directors or big shareholders of electronic firms have reported selling their shareholdings, indicating they are optimistic about their own firms' outlook," Yang said.
"The more rational institutional investors, which had dumped electronics recently, are having second thoughts after seeing the relatively unrational rally in electronics," he said.
